To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cardamom, bay leaves and coriander seeds are good sources of polyphenols and flavonoid and they are good scavengers of free radical and reducing agents.

the total antioxidant capacity of the extracts was in the following order: bay leaf > coriander seeds > cardamom, and the antioxidant capacity of the methanolic extracts was higher than the corresponding aqueous extracts.
The antioxidant activities of cardamom, corriander, and dried bay leaf extracts were evaluated using different in vitro methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the antioxidant capacity and phenolic content of the spices and herbs.
the development of a rapid, sensitive, and reliable method for determination of total antioxidant activity of spices.
the antioxidant capacity and total phenols, tannin, and flavonoid of the spices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antioxidant capacity of a given food depends on the method used for the determination of antioxidant capacity.

the total phenolic content of the spices was not always correlated with their antioxidant activity, which is probably due to the fact that the antioxidant activity is a complex function of several compounds present in the spice extracts.
the antioxidant activity of spices is not directly correlated to their polyphenols, but rather to their phenolic content.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spices are good source of natural antioxidant compounds and they can be utilized as a natural food preservative.
the antioxidant activity of the spices is related to their total polyphenolic content.
the spices and herbs are good sources of antioxidants, which can be used to replace synthetic antioxidants in foods and beverages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the total antioxidant capacity of the extracts was significantly higher than the sum of the individual antioxidant capacities of the phytochemicals.
the total content of flavonoids, phenols and tannins are not good predictors of antioxidant activity.
spices and their extracts are good sources of natural antioxidants and can be used to replace synthetic antioxidants in foods and beverages.
